region.text: 'The territory of Lithuania is whole and indivisible'

ledger.note: 1990: the Supreme Council re-establishes an independent Lithuania on 11 March. The Act 'was approved at 10:44 pm by 124 members of the council while six abstained' and proclaims that 'the execution of the sovereign powers of the State of Lithuania abolished by foreign forces in 1940, is re-established'; the Supreme Soviet 'restored Lithuania's prewar name of the Republic of Lithuania'. The USSR 'demanded revocation of the Act' and 'began applying sanctions' (the Lithuania page: an economic blockade from 20 April 1990, lasting 74 days). The page names the territory 'whole and indivisible' but no boundary; the country is the reading.

region.text: the LRT building and the Vilnius TV Tower

ledger.note: 1991: Soviet forces storm the broadcasting centre in Vilnius on 13 January. 'On 13 January 1991 Soviet forces stormed the LRT building in Vilnius along with the Vilnius TV Tower'; 'Fourteen people were killed and seven hundred injured in what became known as the January Events.' The zone is the two sites; the page gives no wider ground held, and Soviet units stayed in the country until 'the last units of the Russian Army left Lithuania' on 31 August 1993 (Lithuania page).

region.text: the LRT building and the Vilnius TV Tower

ledger.note: 1991: the Soviet Union recognises Lithuania on 6 September. 'on 6 September 1991 Lithuania's independence was recognized by the State Council of the Soviet Union' after the failed August coup; the United Nations admitted Lithuania on 17 September 1991 (the Lithuania page says 17 September in one passage and 18 September in another).

wars.name: January Events

zones.text: the LRT building and the Vilnius TV Tower stormed on 13 January 1991

wars.outcome: Soviet forces seized the broadcasting buildings in Vilnius with 14 dead and about 700 injured; the Soviet Union nevertheless recognised Lithuania on 6 September 1991.
wars.note: A crackdown on an independence already declared (11 March 1990), not a border war; the zone is the two sites, not a front.

certainty.note: 1990-91 is the Lithuanian SSR's republic boundary; the border treaties with Latvia, Belarus and Russia (Kaliningrad) were not on the pages opened (unverified: page budget), but all are drawn as treaty lines.

notes: Cliopatria row 'Republic of Lithuania' 1990..2024 (3 shapes). Dossier starts 11 March 1990 (page) while the lithuanian-soviet-socialist-republic dossier dissolves in March 1990, so the handover is clean; the union-of-soviet-socialist-republics dossier (eu-17) should carry the matching loss and the contest. The Russian garrisons of 1991-93 held bases, not a territory, so no occupation event is written. Pages silent: border treaties and the Latvian cell difference of 1992, Kaliningrad, Neringa, the Klaipeda and Vilnius regions after 1990, a ruler list (no rulers written; the Lithuania page names only Brazauskas as first president, elected 1993). Other recognitions on the Act page: Iceland confirmed its 1922 recognition on 11 February 1991, Denmark recognised on 28 February 1991, the Russian government re-recognised on 27 July 1991, the United States reconfirmed on 2 September 1991.
